answer: Like a jetty that only lets proven boats dock, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a slow-moving glacier of escrowed credit: the stake accrues reputation over time and is slashed if the agent misbehaves. A newcomer starts with a cedar sapling's worth of trust - tiny limits that grow only with verified, useful work. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of stakes and months of waiting, while one honest agent earns its limits back quickly.
